Krishna Sharma

I'm interested in the parts of computing that most abstractions hide: the instructions a processor executes, the bytes moving through memory, the threads competing for resources, and the nanoseconds that separate a good implementation from a great one.

I'm Krishna, a Maths and Computing major from IIT Delhi, currently exploring the intersection of algorithms, systems, and hardware.

This portfolio is my engineering logbook — a place to document what I build, what I learn, and how I push performance further. My interests lie in low-latency systems, GPU programming, CUDA kernel optimization, concurrency, and performance engineering.

I enjoy going beyond abstractions to understand what actually happens under the hood: how CPUs execute instructions, how memory hierarchies shape performance, how threads coordinate, and where hardware becomes the bottleneck.

You'll find experiments, implementations, benchmarks, technical deep dives, and projects exploring the boundaries between software and hardware.

I care about understanding why something is fast, not just making it work. This is an evolving record of my curiosity, progress, and pursuit of building systems that are efficient down to the last cycle.
